Discontinuation of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) due to adverse drug reactions has been analyzed through a meta-analysis of cohort studies, as published in Annals of Medicine in 2023. 2. A study conducted in São Paulo, Brazil, evaluated adherence to HIV PEP in a specialized healthcare service, as reported in the Journal of Infection in Developing Countries in 2023. 3. A multivariate regression analysis of a five-year prospective cohort study examined adherence to HIV PEP, as detailed in the Journal of Infection in 2018. 4. Research in Southern Africa assessed healthcare practitioners' and students' knowledge, attitudes, and adherence to PEP, as published in Health SA in 2022. 5. A North American cohort study investigated adherence to PEP and the incidence of HIV seroconversion, with findings published in PLOS One in 2015. 6. A cohort study at Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra, Ghana, explored adverse events and adherence to HIV PEP, as reported in BMC Public Health in 2015. 7. A qualitative study examined patient acceptance and adherence to HIV PEP following sexual assault, as published in Global Qualitative Nursing Research in 2021. 8. A randomized non-inferiority trial compared standard versus enhanced risk reduction and adherence counseling for individuals receiving PEP after sexual exposure to HIV, as detailed in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2011. 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued clinical guidelines for responding to children and adolescents who have been sexually abused, accessible online as of June 2024. 10. WHO has also developed protocols for the clinical management of rape and intimate partner violence survivors in humanitarian settings, available online as of June 2024. 11. WHO guidelines address responding to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women, with clinical and policy recommendations accessible online as of June 2024. 12. The SEARCH SAPPHIRE study evaluated the uptake of a patient-centered dynamic choice model for HIV prevention in rural Kenya and Uganda, as published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2023. 13. A novel community-based HIV PEP program in rural Kenya and Uganda was assessed for uptake and outcomes, with findings published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2021. 14. A web-based cross-sectional study in China explored the uptake and outcomes of non-occupational PEP use through an online medical platform, as reported in the Journal of Medical Internet Research in 2023. 15. A study in Lusaka, Zambia, assessed the feasibility of police-initiated HIV PEP for sexual violence survivors, as published in BMC Proceedings in 2015. 16. Research in New York City examined sexual and gender minority individuals' interest in sexual health services at collective sex venues, as reported in AIDS and Behavior in 2023. 17. A modeling analysis evaluated the potential cost-effectiveness of community availability of tenofovir, lamivudine, and dolutegravir for HIV prevention and treatment in Africa, as published in The Lancet Global Health in 2023. 18. An observational study in Zimbabwe explored the rise in pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake among female sex workers during COVID-19, as reported in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2021. 19. WHO has issued global recommendations and guidelines on task shifting, accessible online as of June 2024. 20. A study highlighted the role of pharmacists in improving patient access to HIV PEP, as published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases in 2020. 21. Research demonstrated improvements in HIV screening follow-up with emergency department pharmacists dispensing PEP, as reported in the Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy in 2020. 22. Training non-medical prescribers (NMPs) to prescribe PEPSE (post-exposure prophylaxis following sexual exposure) has improved accessibility, as detailed in HIV Medicine in 2018. 23. A pilot study extension in Kenya examined pharmacy-based PrEP delivery, with findings presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in 2023. 24. A study in Ontario assessed the potential for nurse-led HIV preand post-exposure prophylaxis, as published in the Canadian Journal of Nursing Research in 2021. 25. A Cochrane review evaluated task shifting from doctors to non-doctors for initiating and maintaining antiretroviral therapy, as published in 2014. 26. Research in Africa examined the clinical outcomes and self-efficacy of nurses managing HIV care, as reported in AIDS Care in 2014. 27. A study in Kisumu, Kenya, explored adolescent girls' and young women's experiences with pharmacy-based PrEP delivery, as published in the Journal of the International Association of Providers of AIDS Care in 2023. 28. Community pharmacies' role in providing access to HIV PEP was examined in a study published in the Journal of Community Health in 2023. 29. The impact of Senate Bill 159 on the provision of HIV preand post-exposure prophylaxis in Sacramento, California, was assessed, as reported in the Journal of Investigative Medicine in 2023. 30. WHO has provided systematic review findings, GRADE tables, and PEP dosage guidelines in its web annexes, accessible online as of June 2024.
